claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 exhibits a hierarchical heterostructure at room temperature.
Complex interfacial features influence the overall mechanical response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Targeted molecular-dynamics simulations can capture heterointerface bond-breaking events.
Targeted molecular-dynamics simulations can capture dislocation nucleation at critical heterointerfaces.
Atomic-scale bonding and local rearrangements at heterointerfaces mediate the transition from localized plasticity to bulk mechanical response.
Parameters derived from molecular dynamics, including local stiffness and plasticity or yield thresholds, can be transferred into continuum simulations.
An experimentally calibrated transfer function can upscale heterointerface behavior into effective continuum parameters.
Iterative experimental calibration will improve the transfer of molecular-dynamics parameters to the continuum model.
Directly incorporating interfacial physics into the bulk simulation will maintain high predictive accuracy.
Directly incorporating interfacial physics through targeted molecular dynamics will reduce computational cost.
The hybrid framework will predict Young's modulus for HfNbTiVAl10 within 10% of independent experimental measurements.
The hybrid framework will predict yield strength for HfNbTiVAl10 within 10% of independent experimental measurements.
The hybrid framework will predict fracture toughness for HfNbTiVAl10 within 10% of independent experimental measurements.
The hybrid framework will reduce simulation time by roughly 70% relative to conventional continuum finite-element simulations.
Established continuum finite-element simulations require exhaustive meshing and extensive computation.
Established continuum finite-element simulations may neglect fine-scale interfacial physics.
Neglect of fine-scale interfacial physics results in lower predictive accuracy and longer simulation times.
The framework may fail when sampled heterointerfaces are not representative of the material's heterogeneity.
The framework may fail under extreme strain rates or temperatures that deviate from room-temperature conditions.
